# `armada user`

<!-- Generated by `make docs` from the commands; do not edit. -->

[All commands](armada.md)

Users are people. Each has a certificate of their own and holds roles:
viewer, deployer, or admin in a space (viewer also over the whole cluster),
space-creator, or cluster-admin. Only cluster-admin manages access;
`armada role list` shows the roles and who holds them.

Also: `users`.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`armada user create`](#armada-user-create) | Create a user with a certificate of their own |
| [`armada user credentials`](#armada-user-credentials) | Write a new client config for a user, revoking their older certificates |
| [`armada user delete`](#armada-user-delete) | Delete a user and revoke every certificate of it |
| [`armada user list`](#armada-user-list) | List users and their roles |
| [`armada user renew`](#armada-user-renew) | Renew the user certificate in your client config |
| [`armada user show`](#armada-user-show) | Show a user's roles and allowed node labels |
| [`armada user update`](#armada-user-update) | Replace the node labels a user's apps may require |

## `armada user create`

Create a user and write their client config to FILE: a certificate under
their own name (one year) for a key made here. Give them FILE privately; they
keep it as ~/.armada/config, mode 0600. --role gives a first role (in
--space for viewer, deployer, and admin); give more with
`armada role grant`. A user with no role can only renew.

```
armada user create NAME -o FILE [--role ROLE [--space P]] [--allow-label KEY=VALUE]... [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
armada user create ana -o ana.config --role deployer --space shop
armada user create ops -o ops.config --role cluster-admin
armada user create ops -o ops.config --role cluster-admin --ssh ops@bastion.example.com
```

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--allow-label stringArray` | a node label KEY=VALUE its apps' placement may require (repeat for more) |
| `-o`, `--output string` | client config file to create |
| `--role string` | a first role: viewer, deployer, admin (with --space), space-creator, or cluster-admin |
| `--ssh ssh -W` | reach the servers through this SSH host ([user@]host or a ~/.ssh/config alias): ssh -W to their private addresses, mTLS inside |

## `armada user credentials`

Make a key here and a new certificate for user NAME (one year), and write
their client config to FILE. Certificates the user was given before stop
working: use it when a key is lost or leaked.

```
armada user credentials NAME -o FILE [flags]
```

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-o`, `--output string` | client config file to create |
| `--ssh ssh -W` | reach the servers through this SSH host ([user@]host or a ~/.ssh/config alias): ssh -W to their private addresses, mTLS inside |

## `armada user delete`

Revoke every certificate of the user, at once and on every server, and
take its roles back. You cannot delete yourself.

```
armada user delete NAME --yes [flags]
```

Also: `rm`.

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--yes` | confirm deleting |

## `armada user list`

List users and their roles.

```
armada user list [flags]
```

Also: `ls`.

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-o`, `--output string` | output format: text or json (default `text`) |

## `armada user renew`

Get a new one-year certificate for a new key, under the same name, and
rewrite the client config (--config, default ~/.armada/config, else
/etc/armada/admin.config, which needs sudo). Run it before the current
certificate expires: an expired one cannot renew. `armadad doctor` warns 30
days ahead. The old certificate stays valid until it expires. For one that
has expired, run `armadad user renew` as root on a server.

```
armada user renew
```

## `armada user show`

Show a user's roles and allowed node labels.

```
armada user show NAME [flags]
```

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-o`, `--output string` | output format: text or json (default `text`) |

## `armada user update`

Replace the node label values the apps a user deploys may name in
placement.require (armada.* labels are always allowed): restricted nodes
can be kept for some spaces. Roles change with `armada role grant` and `armada role revoke`.

```
armada user update NAME (--allow-label KEY=VALUE... | --clear-labels) [flags]
```

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--allow-label stringArray` | a node label KEY=VALUE its apps' placement may require (repeat for more) |
| `--clear-labels` | allow no node labels |
